headline: Seven Majors Below Their 200-Day Lines, But Alt Momentum and Exchange Flows Tell Different Stories
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it settles the argument before anything else gets said: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, BNB, DOGE and ADA are all trading below their 200-day moving averages, and none show a golden cross. That is not a mixed picture, it's a uniform one. BTC sits 48.2% off its 12-month high of $124,773.51, ETH is down 60.2% from $4,817.76, and the drawdowns get progressively steeper down the cap table: SOL -69.9%, XRP -67.1%, DOGE -75.7%, ADA -81.8%. When every asset in the set is under its long-term trendline, you're not picking winners and losers, you're reading depth of a broader retracement.

Momentum tells a more interesting story than trend does today. RSI readings cluster in the mid-40s to high-50s, nobody is overbought or oversold, so this isn't a market screaming for relief in either direction. But MACD is split: BTC, ETH, SOL and XRP sit below their signal lines while BNB, DOGE and ADA sit above. ADA is the standout, up 7.95% on the day with RSI at 56.7 and MACD bullish, all while still 81.8% off its high. That's a short-term momentum thrust inside a long-term downtrend, worth naming as a divergence rather than a trend change: price recovering faster than the 200-day structure has repaired itself.

Positioning adds texture. Funding is cheap across the board (BTC annualized at 6.6%, ETH at just 1.1%, DOGE at 7.2%) except SOL, where funding runs negative at -2.2%, meaning short holders are the ones paying to stay in the trade. Yet long/short account ratios are stacked long everywhere: SOL at 2.74, XRP at 2.97, DOGE at 3.63. That combination, negative funding but heavily long accounts on SOL, is a genuine split between what the aggregate book pays and what the average account is positioned for. Liquidations lean instructive too: ETH saw $8.9M in short liquidations against $6.96M in longs over 22 hours despite a modest 0.44% gain, while BTC's $6.7M in long liquidations slightly outpaced $6.0M in shorts. Neither side is getting flushed hard; open interest of $1.99B on BTC and $1.38B on ETH sits well within normal ranges, not the kind of crowded, over-levered setup that tends to break violently.

Flows are where the tension sharpens. Whales moved a net $112.7M of BTC onto exchanges over the last 24 hours, with the single largest transfer being $193.7M to Kraken, a move that typically signals intent to sell or at minimum reduce cold-storage exposure. At the same time, large USDT transfers landed on OKEx ($187.9M) and Bitfinex ($119.9M), stablecoin firepower parked on venues rather than deployed. The weekly net figures ($797M, -$156M, -$336M, $1.16B) swing in both directions with no consistent lean, so calling this a trend would be overreaching; it's noise with occasional large prints, not a settled current. On the ETF side, BTC funds took in $32.1M on 29 Jul but the five-session net is -$494.4M with only one day pointing the same direction as today, so the single green print sits inside a heavier outflow stretch. ETH ETFs bled $32.9M on the same day, with a five-session net of -$56.2M. Stablecoin float itself is down 1.6% over 30 days, a mild contraction in the dry powder pool even as fear readings sit elevated.

Sentiment is the foil here, and it disagrees with the tape in a small but real way. The Fear & Greed gauge reads 28, still labeled Fear, sitting near the top of its own 30-day range of 11 to 33. That's a crowd that's been more afraid recently than it is right now, even as total market cap rose 1.35% on the day and ADA posted a near-8% move. The prices moved before the mood did. What's worth watching from here: whether BTC reclaims its 200-day line or whether the current sub-200-day alignment holds across the majors, whether the five-session ETF net turns positive on more than one day at a time, and whether the whale exchange-inflow pattern on BTC persists or reverses toward outflows, since one day of net inflow to exchanges is a data point, not yet a direction.
